note: Every entry lists a source actually fetched over live egress by po03-worker-a5. observed_at is the UTC date the page was retrieved during this commission. Text under evidence_snippet is a short verbatim excerpt confirming the claim was read, not paraphrased from memory.

a5-u01.prediction: A fault class is survivable by a durable-execution style custody engine iff the specific invariant it depends on is present: idempotency/dedup key for duplicate-effect faults, fence token for stale-writer-after-eviction faults, and an append-only history (outbox/event-log) for crash-and-replay faults. Removing the invariant a fault class depends on makes that class unsurvivable while leaving unrelated invariants intact does not fix it.

sources.claim: Durable workflow engines rebuild state by replaying a complete, ordered Event History; a Workflow must be deterministic given that history.
sources.evidence_snippet: Because the Workflow is re-executed to rebuild its state: It has to make the same decisions when given the same history, which makes a Workflow deterministic.

sources.claim: AWS Step Functions documents an explicit exactly-once vs at-least-once distinction tied directly to whether actions are idempotent.
sources.evidence_snippet: Standard Workflows follow an exactly-once model... Express Workflows use an at-least-once model... better suited for orchestrating idempotent actions.

sources.claim: A fencing token (a monotonically increasing number issued at lock/lease acquisition) is the standard fix for a paused/stale client committing after its lease expired.
sources.evidence_snippet: The fix for this problem is actually pretty simple: you need to include a fencing token with every write request to the storage service.

a5-u02.prediction: Under injected callback loss, a content-addressed custody design (result committed to durable, independently re-readable storage keyed by content hash) recovers a materially higher fraction of results than a message-passing design (result only reachable via a single in-flight callback).

sources.claim: Content-addressable storage keys data by the hash of its own content, so any party holding the key can independently re-fetch and verify the content, with no dependency on the writer's delivery channel.
sources.evidence_snippet: Git is a content-addressable filesystem... you can insert any kind of content into a Git repository, for which Git will hand you back a unique key you can use later to retrieve that content.

a5-u03.prediction: Two independently frozen review methodologies applied blind to the same seeded-defect corpus find a non-identical set of defect classes (neither is a subset of the other), so pooling both catches strictly more than either alone.

sources.claim: The founding conjecture of N-version programming is that independently produced implementations from the same spec fail differently, so diversity reduces correlated (identical) defects.
sources.evidence_snippet: the central conjecture that the "independence of programming efforts will greatly reduce the probability of identical software faults"

sources.claim: Real-world lightweight code review at scale is the deployed practice this hypothesis generalizes from; it does not itself measure cross-model-family diversity.
